title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section (9), 'Une conjecture arithmético-géométrique', is the first formulation in this manuscript of an anabelian characterisation of Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q) through moduli of curves. It continues the previous page, which treated the types T_{0,ν} and the action of S_ν × Γ.

Setup. Fix g, ν ≥ 0. M_{g,ν} is the moduli 'type' (stack) over Q of relative smooth proper curves with connected fibres of genus g, with ν sections that are disjoint in every fibre. The excluded cases (g,ν) = (0,0), (0,1), (0,2), (1,0) are exactly the non-hyperbolic ones (2g−2+ν ≤ 0). Outside them the type is a Deligne–Mumford 'multiplicité', which he says is parallel to the notion of orbifold.

Three maps. Take a geometric point ξ, i.e. a curve X over Q̄ with marked points x_1,…,x_ν.
- (*) The arithmetic fundamental group π_1(M_{g,ν/Q}, ξ) maps to Autextlac°(π̂_1(X−{x_i})). These are outer automorphisms of the profinite surface group that preserve each conjugacy class of inertia ('lacets') around each x_i, without permuting the punctures.
- (**) The geometric fundamental group π_1(M_{g,ν}⊗Q̄, ξ) maps to Autextlac°°. These are 'strict' automorphisms that also respect the Tate module T = Ẑ(1) acting on the inertia groups: each inertia generator goes to a conjugate of itself, not of a cyclotomic power. Equivalently, these are the automorphisms with trivial 'cyclotomic character'.
- (***) The transcendental, discrete version: π_1 of the analytic stack maps to Autextlac°°(π_1^{top}(X−{x_i})), which is the Teichmüller (mapping class) group Γ_{g,ν}. By the Dehn–Nielsen–Baer theorem this is an isomorphism.

What the next page does. It builds a map from the homotopy exact sequence
1 → π_1(M_{g,ν}⊗Q̄) → π_1(M_{g,ν/Q}) → Γ → 1
to
1 → T̂_{g,ν} → Autextlac°(π̂) → (quotient) → 1.
He wishes the middle vertical arrow to be an isomorphism. That would characterise Γ as Autextlac°(π̂)/T̂_{g,ν}, a purely 'anabelian' group. A margin variant replaces Autextlac°(π̂) by the normaliser of T̂_{g,ν} in it. For (0,3) the statement collapses to Γ ≅ Autextlac°(π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞})), which he had already considered. A margin note admits an error, or at least a doubt, in that case. He also flags that 'strict' and the compatibility with orientations of loops still need to be made precise.

Purpose. To realise Gal(Q̄/Q) as an automorphism group of a single profinite surface group with inertia structure, uniformly in (g,ν). This is a precursor of the Teichmüller-tower programme of Esquisse d'un programme (1984).
errors: Passing from (***) (discrete, an isomorphism by Dehn–Nielsen–Baer) to an isomorphism in (**) (profinite) is not automatic. Injectivity of Γ̂_{g,ν} → Out(π̂_{g,ν}) is the congruence subgroup property for mapping class groups. It is known for g ≤ 2 (Asada, Boggi, Hoshi–Mochizuki among others) and open in general. Surjectivity onto the strict inertia-preserving automorphisms is a further nontrivial claim. The page and the next one seem to treat the profinite isomorphism as following from the discrete one.

For (g,ν) = (0,3) the conjecture reads Γ ≅ Autextlac°(π̂_{0,3}). Faithfulness of the Galois action is Belyi's theorem (1979). Surjectivity is not known and is widely doubted: the image lies in Drinfeld's GT̂, and whether GT̂ = Γ is open. Grothendieck himself notes in the margin that he is making an error in this case.

The definition of the decorations ° and °° is incomplete, as his own margin note says. One must specify that inertia classes may go to Ẑ^*-powers in °, with the same exponent for all punctures (a cyclotomic-type character), whereas °° requires the exponent 1. Without the common-exponent condition the target group is too large.

Minor: the exceptional list should be justified by hyperbolicity (2g−2+ν > 0). For (1,0) one would also need to handle the generic automorphism (the elliptic involution), and the next page treats only the hyperbolic range.

ideas.what: Outer Galois representation of π_1(M_{g,ν/Q}) on the profinite fundamental group of the universal punctured curve, landing in the inertia-preserving outer automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Universal monodromy / outer pro-mapping-class representation; 'Ihara–Oda' setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1985–86), Oda, Matsumoto, Nakamura (late 1980s–1990s); Grothendieck in Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), sections on the Teichmüller tower and the action of Gal(Q̄/Q); also the 1981 letter to Faltings (1983) in spirit

ideas.what: Distinction between automorphisms preserving inertia up to a cyclotomic twist (°) and strictly (°°, compatible with T = Ẑ(1)), with the geometric part landing in the strict group
ideas.modern_name: Out^I versus Out^{I,1}; cyclotomic character of inertia-preserving automorphisms ('quasi-special/special' automorphisms)

ideas.what: Comparison with the discrete Teichmüller group via Dehn–Nielsen–Baer: the mapping class group equals the type-preserving outer automorphisms of the surface group
Conjecture that π_1(M_{g,ν/Q}) ≅ Autextlac°(π̂_{g,ν}), or the normaliser of Γ̂_{g,ν} in it, giving Γ = Autextlac°/Γ̂_{g,ν} for each hyperbolic (g,ν)
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian characterisation of G_Q; closely related to the Ihara/Oda–Matsumoto (I/OM) conjecture and to the GT̂ = G_Q question
ideas.usually_credited_to: Esquisse (1984) in tower form; Ihara (question about Out of π̂(P^1−3pts)); Oda–Matsumoto; Pop (proof of I/OM-type statements)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse states the tower-level hope; the per-(g,ν) normaliser formulation is not known to me in published texts

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, per single (g,ν), the conjecture that the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{g,ν} equals the inertia-preserving outer automorphism group of π̂_{g,ν}, or the normaliser of the geometric part in it. This is a 'one-level' version of the later tower or GT conjectures. The normaliser variant, written on the next page, compares directly with later results computing centralisers and normalisers of pro-mapping class groups in Out(π̂) (Hoshi–Mochizuki, Minamide–Nakamura). The archival per-level formulation predates those results and is not usually cited as their source.
missed.quote: On aimerait que la flèche ... soit un iso. Cela donnerait une caractérisation de Γ comme Autext lac°(π_1(X∖{x_1,…,x_ν})^)/T̂_{g,ν}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It situates the origin of the Ihara/Oda–Matsumoto-type and GT̂ questions in Grothendieck's c.1980–81 notes in an explicit single-level form, including the normaliser variant. It also shows an early awareness that (0,3) is problematic.

missed.claim: The page implicitly needs the profinite congruence subgroup property for mapping class groups to pass from Dehn–Nielsen–Baer to the profinite isomorphism. The page does not flag this; the problem was later posed explicitly (Ihara, Oda, Boggi).
missed.quote: (***) π_1(M^-_{g,ν};ξ) → Autextloc°° ... = Γ_{g,ν} (Teichmüller) dont on sait ... qu'il est un isomorphisme
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical: the congruence subgroup problem is hidden inside Grothendieck's first formulation. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: The overall idea (G_Q characterised anabelianly via inertia-preserving outer automorphisms on moduli of curves) is known from Esquisse and later work by Ihara, Drinfeld, Nakamura and Pop. What is notable is the explicit, dated pre-Esquisse formulation at each single level (g,ν), the °/°° (cyclotomic versus strict) distinction, the normaliser variant, and Grothendieck's own doubt about the (0,3) case. These are interesting unpublished details, not unknown mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'Autextloc' should read 'Autext lac' (lac = lacets, i.e. inertia loops), consistent with the next page.
'ce type est associé à une itération d'algébriques' is probably 'une multiplicité algébrique' (Grothendieck's term for a DM stack), or similar.
'notion parallèle = symbole' is likely 'notion parallèle = orbifold' (or 'V-variété').
'l'exposant' is uncertain; the sense is 'the curve (over Q̄) corresponding to the point of M_{g,ν}(Q̄) with ν marked points associated to ξ'.
In (**), M̄_{g,ν} denotes M_{g,ν}⊗Q̄ (the geometric fundamental group), not a compactification.
In (***), M^-_{g,ν} denotes the transcendental/analytic object; the parenthesis 'théorie ...' is plausibly a reference to Teichmüller/Nielsen theory.
T = Tate(Q̄) means the Tate module Ẑ(1).
